newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ eases doctors' rules on sex with patients.
newsitem.headline: NZ eases doctors' rules on sex with patients.

text.p: New Zealand's Medical Association has made it possible for doctors to have sexual relationships with their former patients, medical officials said on Monday.
The association will now allow a doctor to have a sexual relationship with a former patient providing the treatment was brief, of a minor nature or in the distant past.
Doctors had been forbidden to have sexual relations with existing or former patients under any circumstances.
Medical Association chairman Brian Linehan told Reuters on Monday the change was more a clarification than a relaxation of the rules.
"In the past, these things would still be raised as a defence, but there was less definition around what was a reasonable defence.
"The code recognises that sometimes a relationship can subsequently develop, and the previous doctor-patient relationship may not have been as important," Linehan said.

Sex with current patients was unacceptable, he added. Also, if the patient had been dependent on the doctor, as in psychiatric treatment, the doctor was obliged not to exploit that relationship, no matter how much time had passed.
Women's Health Action spokeswoman Judi Strid said women's groups were concerned they had not been consulted about the change and said it remained unclear what was acceptable and what was not.
